name: Profit or loss for a period
formula: Profit = Total revenue - Total expenses (a negative result is a loss)
terms: Revenue = income of the period; expenses = costs of the period
note: Revenue ₹6,00,000, expenses ₹5,40,000: profit ₹60,000.

name: Cost benefit analysis
formula: Net benefit = Sum of benefits of an action - Costs of taking that action
terms: Benefits and costs of the decision being analysed
note: Listed among new fields of accounting.

name: Capital after drawings (entity concept)
formula: Closing capital = Capital introduced - Drawings
terms: Drawings = owner's withdrawals for personal use

name: Cost of an asset (cost concept)
formula: Cost = Purchase price + Transport + Installation + Repairs or other costs to make it ready to use
terms: All outlays until the asset is ready for use

name: Revenue on a long-term contract
formula: Revenue realised = % of contract completed x Total contract revenue
terms: Exception to revenue recognition concept
note: 10% x ₹20 lakh = ₹2 lakh.

name: Revenue on instalment sale
formula: Revenue realised in a period = Instalments collected in that period
terms: Exception to revenue recognition concept
note: 12 instalments of ₹1,500: ₹1,500 per month.

name: Accrual concept recognition
formula: Revenue = Total sales value (received or not); Cost = Total cost incurred (paid or not)
terms: Cash received or paid is irrelevant

name: Matching concept profit
formula: Profit = Units sold x Selling price - Units sold x Cost per unit - Expenses of the period (accrued)
terms: Only cost of goods actually sold is matched; period expenses on accrual

name: Annual charge under going concern
formula: Annual charge = Cost of asset / Years of use
terms: Spreads cost over the years the asset earns revenue

name: Accounting equation
formula: Assets = Liabilities + Capital (A = L + C)
terms: A assets, L liabilities, C capital (owner's equity)
note: Also called the Balance Sheet Equation.

name: Balancing an account
formula: Balance c/d = larger side total - smaller side total, written on the smaller side
terms: c/d carried down; brought down next period as b/d on the larger side
note: Debit side larger gives a debit balance. Only asset, liability and capital accounts are balanced.

name: Net invoice amount after trade discount
formula: Amount = Sum(quantity x rate) x (1 - trade discount %)
terms: Used for purchases, sales and return books

name: Trial balance difference to suspense
formula: Suspense A/c opening = Total debits - Total credits of the trial balance (on the shorter side)
terms: Excess credit is put on the debit side of Suspense A/c, and vice versa
note: After all one-sided errors are rectified the Suspense A/c balances.

name: Posting to the wrong side
formula: Correction = 2 x amount
terms: An amount posted to the debit instead of the credit of an account
note: Sheet example: Rs 20,000 credit purchase posted to debit of Raghu: credit Raghu Rs 40,000, debit Suspense Rs 40,000.

name: Net casting error from carry forward
formula: Net over/undercast = sum of overcasts - sum of undercasts
terms: Wrong page totals carried forward in a subsidiary book
note: Sheet example: undercast Rs 200 and overcast Rs 600 give net overcast Rs 400 in sales.

name: Maturity date of a bill
formula: Maturity date = date of drawing + term of bill + 3 days of grace
terms: Term in days: count exact days; term in months: same date in the later month
note: 5 March + 30 days = 4 April + 3 = 7 April; 5 March + 1 month = 5 April + 3 = 8 April.

name: Discount on discounting a bill
formula: Discount = Bill amount x Rate p.a. x Unexpired months / 12
terms: Rate charged by bank; period from discounting to maturity

name: Cash received on discounting
formula: Bank proceeds = Bill amount - Discount
terms: Discount is debited to Discount A/c (expense)

name: Discount on endorsement in full settlement
formula: Discount received = Debt settled - Bill amount endorsed
terms: Endorser credits Discount Received; endorsee debits Discount Allowed
note: Rs 8,250 debt settled by an Rs 8,000 bill: discount Rs 250.

name: Valuation of finished goods and WIP
formula: Inventory value = Lower of (Cost, NRV)
terms: NRV = net realisable value

name: Valuation of raw material
formula: RM value = Cost, if FG sell at or above cost; else Replacement cost
terms: Replacement cost = cost of buying the next best substitute

name: Net realisable value
formula: NRV = Estimated selling price - Estimated cost of completion - Estimated costs to sell
terms: Costs to sell: brokerage, sales commission

name: Inventory write-down
formula: Written down value = Cost of inventory - NRV
terms: Applies when NRV < cost
note: AS 2 does not allow reversal; Ind AS 2 does

name: Cost of inventory
formula: Cost = Cost of purchase + Cost of conversion + Other costs
terms: Other costs: bringing inventory to present location and condition

name: Cost of purchase
formula: Cost of purchase = Purchase price + Import duties + Transport + Handling - Trade discounts and rebates
terms: Cash discount is not deducted

name: Cost of conversion
formula: Cost of conversion = Direct labour + Fixed production overheads (normal capacity) + Variable production overheads (actual production)
terms: Less value of any by-product (summary chart)

name: Fixed overhead absorption rate
formula: Rate = Fixed production overheads / Normal capacity, if actual <= normal; Fixed overheads / Actual output, if actual > normal
terms: Unabsorbed (normal rate x shortfall) goes to P&L
note: ₹18 lakh / 1 lakh units = ₹18; at 90,000 units absorb ₹16.2 lakh, ₹1.8 lakh to P&L; at 1.2 lakh units rate ₹15

name: Weighted average cost
formula: Average cost per unit = Total cost of goods purchased / Total units
terms: Used for both issues and closing inventory

name: FIFO closing inventory
formula: Closing inventory = remaining units valued at the latest purchase prices (earliest units issued first)
terms: FIFO = first in, first out

name: Interest income (time proportion)
formula: Interest recognised = Total interest x (Months elapsed in the period / Total months)
terms: Time proportion basis under AS 9
note: ₹1,200 over 12 months from 1 Jan, year ending March: 1,200 / 12 x 3 = ₹300. Loan ₹20,000 at 2% for 4 years: ₹1,600 total, ₹400 a year

name: Revenue of a commission agent
formula: Revenue = Commission rate x Gross value of bookings
terms: Only the commission is revenue

name: Interest in an instalment sale
formula: Interest = Total instalments - Cash sale price
terms: Sale price excl. interest recognised on date of sale

name: Subscription revenue
formula: Revenue = Sum of sales value of items delivered (varying value); or Total subscription / periods, straight-line (equal value)
terms: Publications subscription

name: Cost of acquired PPE
formula: Cost = Purchase price (incl. import duties, non-refundable taxes, less trade discounts, rebates, scrap value) + Directly attributable costs + PV of dismantling/restoration costs
terms: Directly attributable: site preparation, delivery, installation, testing net of sample proceeds, professional fees, employee benefits
note: Exclude govt grants, admin overheads, cash discounts, deferred-credit interest.

name: Testing cost capitalised
formula: Testing cost - Net proceeds from sale of samples produced during testing
terms: Samples produced while bringing the asset to working condition

name: Self-constructed asset: capitalised interest
formula: Interest = Loan x Rate x (Construction months till ready for use / 12)
terms: Only the period until the asset is ready for use

name: Exchange of assets
formula: Cost of asset received = Fair value of asset given up (+ cash paid); if that fair value is unknown, fair value of asset received
terms: Applies when the exchange has commercial substance and a fair value is reliably measurable

name: Deferred payment
formula: Cost of PPE = Cash price equivalent; (Total deferred payments - Cash price) = interest, not capitalised
terms: Example: 180 lakh over 3 years vs 150 lakh cash: cost 150 lakh

name: Replacement of a part
formula: New carrying amount = Carrying amount + Cost of new part - Carrying amount of replaced part

name: Major inspection
formula: New carrying amount = Carrying amount + Cost of new inspection - Remaining carrying amount of previous inspection

name: Cost model carrying amount
formula: Carrying amount = Cost - Accumulated depreciation - Accumulated impairment loss

name: Revaluation model carrying amount
formula: Carrying amount = Fair value at revaluation date - Subsequent accumulated depreciation - Subsequent impairment loss

name: Revaluation surplus
formula: Revaluation surplus = Fair value - (Cost - Accumulated depreciation)
terms: Credited to revaluation reserve (OCI) on first revaluation

name: Proportional method of revaluation
formula: Restated gross = Gross x (Revalued amount / Carrying amount); Restated AD = AD x (Revalued amount / Carrying amount)
note: Elimination method: gross = revalued amount, AD = nil.

name: Depreciable amount
formula: Depreciable amount = Cost (or revalued amount) - Residual value
terms: Residual value capped at 5% of original cost under Companies Act 2013 Schedule II

name: Rate of depreciation (SLM)
formula: Rate % = Annual depreciation / Depreciable amount x 100
note: The sheet's printed formula is blank; rate derived from its worked example.

name: Straight line method
formula: Annual depreciation = (Cost - Residual value) / Useful life

name: Diminishing balance (WDV) method
formula: Depreciation = (Opening NBV - Residual value) x Rate %; final year = Opening NBV - Residual value
terms: NBV = cost less depreciation charged so far
note: As taught in the sheet: 2,000, residual 500, 50%: 750, 375, last year 375.

name: Units of production method
formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Residual value) x Output this period / Total expected output
note: Zero if no production.

name: Revised estimate of life or value
formula: New annual depreciation = (Carrying amount at change + any increase - Residual value) / Revised remaining useful life

name: Component significance (Schedule II)
formula: Depreciate separately if Component cost >= 10% of total cost of the asset
terms: Gear box 5 lakh, engine 2 lakh of 10 lakh car

name: Impairment loss
formula: Impairment loss = Carrying amount - Recoverable amount
terms: Recoverable amount: amount recoverable through use or sale (AS 28 / Ind AS 36)

name: Initial recognition amount
formula: Rupee amount = Foreign currency amount x Exchange rate on transaction date (or average rate)
terms: Transaction-date spot rate

name: Exchange difference on a monetary item
formula: Exchange difference = Foreign currency amount x (Closing or settlement rate - Rate last used)
terms: Rate last used = transaction rate or previous balance sheet rate
note: On a liability, a rise in the rate is a loss; on an asset, a gain. $100 loan 50 to 55 to 56: losses ₹500 then ₹100.

name: Revaluation of a non-monetary asset (AS 11 example)
formula: Revaluation = (Fair value in FC - Cost in FC) x Historical rate; Exchange difference = Fair value in FC x (Closing rate - Historical rate)
terms: FC = foreign currency
note: $100 machine at ₹70 revalued to $105, rate ₹72: revaluation 5 x 70 = ₹350; exchange gain 105 x 2 = ₹210.

name: Capitalisation into depreciable asset
formula: Revised cost = Cost + Exchange loss (or - gain); Depreciation = Revised cost / Remaining useful life
terms: Applies to long-term foreign currency monetary item used for a depreciable asset
note: ₹48 lakh + ₹2 lakh = ₹50 lakh; depreciation 50/10 = ₹5 lakh; WDV ₹45 lakh.

name: FCMITDA amortisation
formula: Amount to P&L for the year = Exchange difference / Balance period of the long-term monetary item
terms: Unamortised balance stays in FCMITDA (Reserves and Surplus)
note: ₹2 lakh / 5 years = ₹0.40 lakh to P&L; ₹1.60 lakh in FCMITDA.

name: Forward contract premium (hedging)
formula: Premium per unit = Forward rate - Spot rate; Total premium = Premium per unit x Contract amount, amortised over the contract period
terms: Forward rate = contracted rate; spot rate = rate on contract date
note: 49.15 - 48.85 = ₹0.30 x $1,00,000 = ₹30,000. Loss for a buyer, gain for a seller.

name: Exchange difference on hedging forward contract
formula: Exchange difference = Contract amount x (Spot rate on reporting/settlement date - Rate at last calculation)
terms: Recognised in P&L at once, not amortised

name: Mark to market (speculative forward contract)
formula: MTM = Contract amount x (Current forward rate for remaining maturity - Rate last used); on early sale, MTM = Selling price - Last forward rate
terms: Rate last used = contract rate at first, then previous MTM rate
note: Contract at 51; forward 54 on 31 March: gain 3 x 100 = 300; 55 on 1 May: gain 1 x 100 = 100. MTM goes to P&L.

name: Proportionate FCTR reclassification (Ind AS 21 partial disposal, control retained)
formula: Amount to P&L = FCTR balance x Stake sold / Stake held
terms: FCTR = Foreign Currency Translation Reserve
note: Sell 5% of a 35% associate: 5/35 = one-seventh of FCTR to P&L. Loss of control or 100% sale: whole FCTR.

name: Cost of investment
formula: Cost = Purchase price + Brokerage + Fees + Duties + Commissions + Misc. acquisition costs
terms: All acquisition charges are capitalised
note: Sheet: shares ₹1,000 + 2% brokerage ₹20 + stamp duty 50 paise per ₹100 (₹5) = ₹1,025

name: Cost when acquired by issuing shares
formula: Cost = Fair value of securities issued + issue expenses + taxes
terms: Fair value of the asset acquired is ignored

name: Cost when acquired in exchange for another asset
formula: Cost = Fair value of asset given up (or fair value of investment received if more clearly evident)

name: Pre-acquisition (accrued) interest
formula: Accrued interest = Face value x Coupon rate x Months since last interest date / 12; Net cost = Cum-interest cost (incl. brokerage, taxes) - Accrued interest
terms: Taxes in the sheet example are computed on price less interest; brokerage on the full price

name: Pre-acquisition dividend
formula: Net cost = Cost - Dividend received out of pre-acquisition profits

name: Rights subscribed
formula: New cost = Old cost + (Rights shares x Rights price)

name: Rights sold (shares bought cum-right)
formula: Reduce cost by (Cost - Ex-right market value), limited to sale proceeds; Balance of proceeds to P&L
terms: If shares were not bought cum-right, all proceeds go to P&L
note: ₹15,000 proceeds: ₹10,000 reduces cost to ₹40,000, ₹5,000 to P&L

name: Average cost with bonus shares
formula: Average cost = Total cost / (Original shares + Bonus shares)
terms: Bonus shares carry nil cost

name: Carrying amount: current investment
formula: Carrying amount = Lower of cost and fair value; write-back on recovery = min(Fair value, Cost) - Written-down amount
terms: Write-back is credited to P&L, capped at cost

name: Carrying amount: long-term investment
formula: Carrying amount = Cost - Decline other than temporary
terms: Temporary declines ignored; non-temporary recovery written back to P&L

name: Profit on disposal
formula: Profit/loss = Net sale proceeds (gross sale - expenses) - Carrying amount of investment sold
terms: Part disposal: carrying amount at average carrying amount; stock-in-trade securities: FIFO or average

name: Reclassification value
formula: LT to current = lower of cost and carrying amount; Current to LT = lower of cost and fair value
terms: At date of transfer

name: Maximum buy-back (resource test)
formula: Buy-back ≤ 25% x (Paid-up capital + Free reserves)
terms: SEBI: on standalone or consolidated, whichever is lower; ≤10% board resolution, >10% special resolution

name: Post buy-back debt-equity ratio
formula: (Secured + Unsecured debt) / (Paid-up capital + Free reserves) ≤ 2:1
terms: Debt includes long and short term; NBFC/HFC subsidiaries excluded but each must be ≤ 6:1 standalone

name: Transfer to Capital Redemption Reserve (Sec 69)
formula: CRR transfer = Number of shares bought back x Face value
terms: When bought back out of free reserves or securities premium

name: Buy-back balance sheet effect
formula: Cash falls by shares x buy-back price; Share capital falls by shares x face value; Reserves fall by shares x premium paid
note: 50 shares at ₹50 (FV ₹10): cash -₹2,500, capital -₹500, reserves -₹2,000

name: EPS after buy-back
formula: EPS = Earnings / Number of shares
terms: Fewer shares after buy-back raise EPS if earnings are constant

name: Promoter holding after buy-back
formula: Promoter % = Promoter shares / (Total shares - Shares cancelled)

name: Tender offer small shareholder reservation
formula: Reserved = max(15% of shares to be bought back, shares entitled as per holding)
terms: Small shareholder: holding ≤ ₹2 lakh at closing price on record date

name: Tender offer escrow
formula: Escrow = 25% of buy-back size up to ₹100 crore + 10% of amount above ₹100 crore

name: Open market utilisation
formula: Minimum use = 75% of buy-back size; at least 40% within first half of buy-back period
note: ₹300 crore: ₹225 crore and ₹120 crore

name: ESOP value at grant (PYQ)
formula: Value of option = Market price at grant date - Exercise price
terms: Price on exercise date is ignored
note: ₹90 - ₹75 = ₹15. EduTap calls this fair value; the same difference is the intrinsic value.

name: Gross Profit
formula: Gross Profit = Sales - COGS
terms: Sales net of sales returns; COGS = cost of goods sold

name: Cost of Goods Sold
formula: COGS = Opening Stock + Purchases + Direct Expenses - Closing Stock
terms: Direct expenses: wages, carriage/freight inwards, factory rent, fuel etc.
note: With no opening or closing stock, COGS = purchases + direct expenses. Net purchases = purchases - purchase returns.

name: Net Profit
formula: Net Profit = Gross Profit + Other Incomes - Indirect Expenses = Total Revenue - Total Expenses
terms: Indirect expenses: salaries, rent, bad debts etc.

name: Gross Profit Ratio
formula: GP Ratio = (Total Revenue - COGS) / Total Revenue x 100
terms: Total revenue = sales
note: From PYQ FIN.S9 solution.

name: Debtors in Balance Sheet
formula: Debtors shown = (Debtors - Provision for doubtful debts) - Discount % x (Debtors - Provision for doubtful debts)
terms: Provision for discount is computed on good debtors only
note: From PYQ FIN.P2 solution.

name: Commission on profit before charging commission
formula: Commission = Profit before commission x Rate of commission / 100
terms: Rate in %

name: Interest on capital
formula: Interest = Opening capital x rate + Additional capital x rate x period from date introduced
terms: Rate given; period in fraction of year
note: Treated as an expense.

name: Accounting equation (Framework)
formula: Assets = Equity + Liabilities; Equity = Assets - Liabilities
terms: Equity = residual interest

name: Operating Profit (EBIT)
formula: Operating Profit = Gross Profit - Operating Expenses
terms: Operating (indirect) expenses: depreciation, office rent, marketing, admin

name: EBITD
formula: EBITD = EBIT + Depreciation
terms: EBIT = operating profit

name: Profit Before Tax
formula: PBT = Operating Profit + Non-Operating Income - Non-Operating Expenses
terms: Non-operating: sale of assets, investment income, loss by fire, interest expense

name: Profit After Tax
formula: PAT = PBT - Tax
terms: Net profit = PAT

name: Net Sales
formula: Net Sales = Sales - Sales Returns

name: Units of production depreciation
formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Residual Value) x Output Produced / Total Output
terms: Total output = expected production capacity

name: Schedule III note threshold
formula: Disclose any item > higher of (1% of Revenue from Operations, ₹1,00,000)
terms: Applies to items of income or expenditure

name: Working Capital
formula: Working Capital = Current Assets - Current Liabilities
terms: CA: cash, receivables, prepaid, inventory; CL: payables, creditors, short-term borrowings

name: Change in working capital
formula: Change in WC = WC (current year) - WC (previous year)
terms: Rise in CA raises WC; rise in CL lowers WC
note: Example: 42,000 - 42,200 = decrease of 200.

name: Horizontal (comparative) % change
formula: % Change = (Current year value - Previous year value) / Previous year value x 100
terms: Absolute change = current - previous

name: Common size percentage
formula: Item % = Item / Base x 100
terms: Base: revenue from operations (P&L) or total assets/liabilities (Balance Sheet)

name: Funds from operations
formula: Funds from Operations = Net Income + Non-cash charges (e.g., Depreciation)
terms: Depreciation is a non-cash loss

name: Fund flow balancing
formula: Sources of Funds - Applications of Funds = Increase (or Decrease) in Working Capital
terms: Positive = increase in WC (shown as application); negative = decrease (shown on sources side)

name: Current ratio
formula: Current assets ÷ Current liabilities
note: Liquidity; 2:1 taken as acceptable. Web source (not EduTap): ICAI BoS ratio material (live.icai.org) and NIOS Accountancy ratios lesson.

name: Quick (acid-test) ratio
formula: (Current assets − Inventories − Prepaid expenses) ÷ Current liabilities
note: Liquidity; 1:1 taken as satisfactory. Web source (not EduTap): ICAI BoS ratio material (live.icai.org) and NIOS Accountancy ratios lesson.

name: Debt-equity ratio
formula: Total debt ÷ Shareholders' equity
note: Leverage. Web source (not EduTap): ICAI BoS ratio material (live.icai.org) and NIOS Accountancy ratios lesson.

name: Proprietary ratio
formula: (Equity share capital + Preference share capital + Reserves and surplus) ÷ Total assets
note: Leverage. Web source (not EduTap): ICAI BoS ratio material (live.icai.org) and NIOS Accountancy ratios lesson.

name: Capital gearing ratio
formula: (Preference share capital + Debentures + Other borrowings) ÷ Equity
note: Leverage. Web source (not EduTap): ICAI BoS ratio material (live.icai.org) and NIOS Accountancy ratios lesson.

name: Interest coverage ratio
formula: EBIT ÷ Interest
note: Coverage. Web source (not EduTap): ICAI BoS ratio material (live.icai.org) and NIOS Accountancy ratios lesson.

name: Debt service coverage ratio
formula: Earnings available for debt service ÷ (Interest + Instalments)
note: Coverage. Web source (not EduTap): ICAI BoS ratio material (live.icai.org) and NIOS Accountancy ratios lesson.

name: Inventory turnover ratio
formula: Cost of goods sold ÷ Average inventory; Average inventory = (Opening + Closing) ÷ 2
note: Activity, in times. Web source (not EduTap): ICAI BoS ratio material (live.icai.org) and NIOS Accountancy ratios lesson.

name: Receivables turnover ratio
formula: Net credit sales ÷ Average receivables
note: Activity, in times. Web source (not EduTap): ICAI BoS ratio material (live.icai.org) and NIOS Accountancy ratios lesson.

name: Average collection period
formula: 12 months (or 360 days) ÷ Receivables turnover
note: Activity. Web source (not EduTap): ICAI BoS ratio material (live.icai.org) and NIOS Accountancy ratios lesson.

name: Payables turnover ratio
formula: Net credit purchases ÷ Average payables
note: Activity. Web source (not EduTap): ICAI BoS ratio material (live.icai.org) and NIOS Accountancy ratios lesson.

name: Return on equity
formula: (EAT − Preference dividend) ÷ Equity shareholders' funds
note: Profitability. Web source (not EduTap): ICAI BoS ratio material (live.icai.org) and NIOS Accountancy ratios lesson.

name: Net profit margin
formula: Net income ÷ Sales
note: Profitability. Web source (not EduTap): ICAI BoS ratio material (live.icai.org) and NIOS Accountancy ratios lesson.

name: Earnings per share
formula: Net profit available to equity shareholders ÷ Weighted average number of equity shares
note: Market. Web source (not EduTap): ICAI BoS ratio material (live.icai.org) and NIOS Accountancy ratios lesson.

name: Price-earnings ratio
formula: Market price per share ÷ EPS
note: Market. Web source (not EduTap): ICAI BoS ratio material (live.icai.org) and NIOS Accountancy ratios lesson.

name: Dividend payout ratio
formula: DPS ÷ EPS
note: Market. Web source (not EduTap): ICAI BoS ratio material (live.icai.org) and NIOS Accountancy ratios lesson.
